title: Identifiability: GPS coordinates reveal child's location patterns
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from child's device can reveal sensitive location information including home address, school, regular routes, and frequent locations, making the child identifiable through their movement patterns.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted with sufficient precision and frequency to enable location tracking

title: Linkability: GPS data can be linked to child's identity
description: The GPS coordinates can be linked to the child's identity through the mobile app backend, potentially enabling correlation with other personal data stored in the system.
assumptions: The backend maintains user profiles that can be correlated with location data

title: Disclosure: Unauthorized access to GPS tracking data
description: Live GPS coordinates could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the backend system is compromised or if access controls are insufficient.
assumptions: The backend has access to the GPS data and may share it with third parties

title: Data Minimization: Excessive GPS data collection
description: Continuous live GPS tracking may collect more location data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The purpose of data collection does not require continuous real-time location tracking

title: Usurpation: Unauthorized device access for GPS spoofing
description: An attacker with physical access to the child's device could potentially spoof or manipulate GPS coordinates, leading to false location reporting.
assumptions: The child's device is accessible to unauthorized persons

title: Unintended Location Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Location pings written to the Location History Store may be accessible to unauthorized third parties or systems, resulting in implicit data disclosure beyond intended recipients.
assumptions: The Location History Store may have access controls that are insufficient, or the data may be shared with external services without proper consent.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [5] about data disclosure; exact tree node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability of Location History to Individual Identity
description: The stored location history can be linked to specific users, potentially revealing patterns of movement and behavior that identify individuals.
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable and can be correlated with user accounts or device identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for linkability threats; exact node may vary.

title: Inference of Sensitive Information from Location Patterns
description: Analysis of location history data may reveal sensitive information such as home/work addresses, religious/political affiliations, or health-related visits.
assumptions: Location patterns can be analyzed to infer sensitive personal information beyond the raw location data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for inference threats; exact node may vary.

title: Unnecessary Location Data Disclosure to Geofencing Engine
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) forwards location pings to the Geofencing Engine (P2). This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal location data is transferred across a process boundary. The threat arises if the disclosure is not strictly necessary for the geofencing functionality, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Location data contains personal information that could be used to track individuals' movements.
uncertainty_note: Assuming location pings contain personal data; severity depends on whether geofencing requires all location data or could use anonymized/aggregated data.

title: Location Data Used for Individual Identification
description: Location pings forwarded from P1 to P2 could be used to identify specific individuals based on their movement patterns and geofencing triggers. This identification threat exists if the geofencing engine correlates location data with user identities.
assumptions: The geofencing engine has access to user identity information that can be correlated with location data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether P2 has access to user identity data; if P2 only processes anonymous location pings, this threat is reduced.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromised During Transfer
description: Location pings transferred from P1 to P2 could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during the data flow. This could result in incorrect geofencing decisions, false alerts, or misleading location-based actions.
assumptions: The data transfer between P1 and P2 is not fully secured against tampering.
uncertainty_note: Assumes standard data transfer security; actual risk depends on implementation of authentication and integrity checks.

title: Zone definitions reveal family member locations
description: The Family Account Store contains geofencing zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) that could identify where family members live, attend school, and visit. This location data can be used to infer family routines and patterns.
assumptions: Zone definitions are stored with family member associations
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 from context as it applies to DataStore->Process flows

title: Unauthorized access to zone configuration data
description: The zone definitions in the Family Account Store could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, exposing sensitive location information about family members.
assumptions: Access controls on DS2 may be inadequate
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 from context as it applies to DataStore->Process flows

title: Zone data linked to other family data
description: The geofencing zone data read by the Geofencing Engine could be linked with other data flows (e.g., family member profiles, activity logs) to create a comprehensive picture of family members' movements and habits.
assumptions: Other data flows exist that contain complementary information
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 from context as it applies to DataStore->Process flows

title: Linkability of Geofencing Notifications
description: Arrival/departure notifications from the Geofencing Engine could be linked across multiple events to reconstruct detailed movement patterns of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information about routines, locations, and activities.
assumptions: Notifications are transmitted in a way that allows correlation across time and events
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree

title: Identification of Child's Location and Movements
description: The geofencing notifications inherently identify the child's location and movement patterns, which could be used to track the child's whereabouts and potentially infer sensitive information about their daily activities and habits.
assumptions: Notifications contain or can be correlated with identifying information about the child
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree

title: Disclosure of Geofencing Notifications to Unauthorized Parties
description: Arrival/departure notifications could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through interception, logging, or improper access controls, exposing the child's location and movement data to entities without legitimate need to know.
assumptions: Notifications are transmitted over networks or stored in systems with potential unauthorized access
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree

title: Usurpation of Geofencing Notification Functionality
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the Geofencing Engine or the child to send false arrival/departure notifications, leading to incorrect alerts or manipulation of the parent's awareness of the child's location.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms for the Geofencing Engine or notification generation are insufficient
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary based on full threat tree

title: Parent identity linked to child profile data
description: The parent's registration data (name, contact info) could be linked to the child's sensitive profile information (name, DOB, school), creating a comprehensive family privacy profile that could be exploited for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The system stores parent and child data in a way that allows correlation
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a general linkability node; specific tree_node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy

title: Child profile data exposed during registration
description: During account registration, the child's personally identifiable information (name, DOB, school) is transmitted to the backend, creating opportunities for interception or unauthorized identification of the child.
assumptions: Data is transmitted in plaintext or insufficiently encrypted during registration flow
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific context may require adjustment

title: Parent identity usurpation during registration
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent during the registration process to create unauthorized child profiles, potentially leading to identity theft or unauthorized access to child-related services.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or bypassable during registration
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific context may require adjustment

title: Child profile data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could disclose the child's sensitive profile data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) to unauthorized third parties, violating privacy expectations and potentially exposing the child to risks.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data sharing policies at the process level
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific context may require adjustment

title: Geofence zone data misrepresented or falsified
description: The system could misrepresent or falsify geofence zone data, potentially leading to incorrect location tracking or privacy implications for the child's actual location patterns.
assumptions: Data integrity mechanisms are weak or data can be tampered with
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a general data deception node; specific context may require adjustment

title: Excessive Personal Data Storage in Family Account Store
description: Backend stores comprehensive account, child profile, and geofence zone data. Risk of storing more personal data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating minimality principle. Child profile data is particularly sensitive and may include unnecessary details.
assumptions: System stores all collected data without strict necessity review
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context about data disclosure; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Family Account Data
description: Personal data (account credentials, child profiles, geofence zones) stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are inadequate. Child profile data is especially sensitive.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly implemented or enforced
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is inferred; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version

title: Data Integrity Risk for Geofence Zone Data
description: Geofence zone data could be tampered with or corrupted, potentially leading to incorrect location-based services or security vulnerabilities. Data integrity is critical for location-based parental controls.
assumptions: Data may be modified without proper integrity checks
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version

title: Location Data Directly Identifies Child
description: The child's current location or location history can be directly linked to the child's identity, enabling identification of the child's movements, routines, and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is stored and processed in a manner that allows correlation with the child's identity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: Location data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: The system may not have sufficient access controls to prevent unauthorized access to location data.

title: Excessive Location History Collection
description: Requesting full location history may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose of viewing current location, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system collects and stores historical location data beyond what is needed for the parent's immediate request.

title: Location Data Used for Identity Impersonation
description: Location data could be misused to impersonate the child, potentially enabling unauthorized access to services or activities.
assumptions: Location data could be combined with other information to create a convincing identity profile.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: Collection and processing of child location data may violate child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) if proper consent and safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: The system may not have adequate consent mechanisms or data protection measures for child data.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Location history data stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized actors or systems without proper authentication and authorization controls.
assumptions: Access controls on the data store are not properly implemented or are bypassed.

title: User Identification via Location Patterns
description: Retrieved location history can be used to identify the user through movement patterns, frequently visited locations, and temporal data.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to enable user identification.

title: Linkability of Location Data to Other Data
description: Location history can be linked with other personal data (e.g., device ID, account info) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Location data is combined with other identifiers in the system.

title: Disclosure of Location History to Unauthorized Parties
description: Location history data could be disclosed to third parties without user consent, violating privacy expectations and regulations.
assumptions: Data sharing mechanisms lack proper consent management.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location to secondary guardian
description: When Parent (EE1) invites a secondary guardian to view child's location, the Mobile App Backend (P1) may disclose the child's location data to the secondary guardian without proper authorization or consent verification. This could expose sensitive location information to parties who may not have legitimate need-to-know.
assumptions: Secondary guardian may have access to child's location without proper consent mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred based on disclosure threat patterns for ExternalEntity->Process flows

title: Location data integrity compromised during transmission
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) may transmit child's location data to the secondary guardian with potential for tampering or manipulation. Location data could be altered, delayed, or falsified during the data flow from EE1 to P1.
assumptions: Data flow between ExternalEntity and Process may lack integrity controls
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard integrity threat node for data flows

title: Secondary guardian impersonation or unauthorized access
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) may be vulnerable to impersonation attacks where an unauthorized party pretends to be a secondary guardian to access child's location data. This could occur during the invitation/authorization process.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not sufficiently verify secondary guardian identity
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard usurpation threat node for process elements

title: Linkability of parent identity to child's location data
description: The Parent (EE1) may inadvertently link their identity to the child's location data when inviting a secondary guardian. This could create a privacy risk where the parent's association with the child's location is exposed to the secondary guardian or other parties.
assumptions: Metadata about the parent-child relationship may be transmitted with location data
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a standard linkability threat node for source elements

title: Child Identification from Live Location Data
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) can identify the specific child from the live location data shared by the backend (P1), potentially revealing the child's identity to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The location data contains sufficient context to identify the child, and the secondary guardian has access to this data.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) may share or disclose the child's live location data to unauthorized third parties, violating the child's privacy expectations.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has the capability to share data externally and may not be bound by strict confidentiality obligations.

title: Linkability of Location Data with Other Information
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) can link the live location data with other available information to build a detailed profile of the child's movements, habits, and routines.
assumptions: The secondary guardian has access to additional data sources that can be correlated with the location data.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Location Sharing
description: Sharing live location data with a secondary guardian may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR, COPPA, or child protection laws, depending on the jurisdiction and consent mechanisms.
assumptions: The data sharing does not have proper parental consent or legal basis, and the secondary guardian's role is not clearly defined in privacy policies.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Even though data is described as 'aggregated', there is a risk that usage and engagement patterns could be linked with other datasets (e.g., device IDs, IP addresses, or other partner data) to re-identify individual users or create detailed user profiles.
assumptions: Partner may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with this analytics data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The advertising/analytics partner may share or sell the received analytics data to additional third parties beyond the original scope of the partnership, potentially exposing user engagement patterns to unauthorized entities.
assumptions: Partner may have business incentives to monetize data beyond the agreed purpose
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected as appropriate node for disclosure threats in Process→ExternalEntity context

title: Excessive Data Collection and Sharing
description: The backend may be sharing more detailed usage and engagement data than necessary for the stated advertising/analytics purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The 'aggregated' description may not reflect actual data granularity being transmitted
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 chosen for data minimization concerns in Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Unintended Data Usage by Partner
description: The advertising/analytics partner may use the received analytics data for purposes beyond the agreed-upon funding of the app's free tier, such as building user profiles for targeted advertising or selling to data brokers.
assumptions: Partner may have broader business objectives that conflict with the stated data-sharing purpose
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 selected for usability/usage concerns in Process→ExternalEntity context

title: Location data linkability to identity
description: The child's location data in the SOS/check-in message could be linked to their identity or other personal data, enabling tracking of movements and patterns.
assumptions: The system stores or logs location data that can be correlated with the child's identity.
uncertainty_note: Using generic threat tree node L.1.1 as context didn't provide specific node for this flow

title: Location data reveals child's whereabouts
description: The current location data in the SOS message can identify the child's physical location, potentially revealing sensitive information about their activities, home address, or school location.
assumptions: Location data is transmitted and stored in a way that preserves geographic precision.
uncertainty_note: Using generic threat tree node I.1.1 as context didn't provide specific node for this flow

title: Child can deny sending SOS message
description: The child may be able to deny or repudiate sending the SOS/check-in message, which could be problematic in emergency situations where proof of message origin is needed.
assumptions: The system does not maintain cryptographic signatures or other non-repudiation mechanisms for the SOS message.
uncertainty_note: Using context node Nr.1 from retrieved knowledge base

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The child's location data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: The system has access controls that may not be properly implemented or enforced.
uncertainty_note: Using generic threat tree node D.1.1 as context didn't provide specific node for this flow

title: Child identity usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the child to send false SOS messages or check-in data, causing false alarms or misleading the parent.
assumptions: The system does not have strong authentication mechanisms to verify the child's identity when sending messages.
uncertainty_note: Using generic threat tree node U.1.1 as context didn't provide specific node for this flow
